Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Transcribe what you can see, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure and method
I read PROMPT.md and packet.json and inspected image-001.png using view_image with detail="original". No proposed identification, earlier transcription, or proposed reading was supplied to this reader. I did not consult a source, search the network, identify a work or author, or open any other image or repository file. The exact model identifier is not exposed to me.

Input inventory (basenames): PROMPT.md; packet.json; image-001.png.
Tool inventory: exec_command (read the two instructions/manifest files and write this response); view_image (original-detail display); functions.exec (tool wrapper); collaboration.send_message (status report, containing no proposed reading).
Output inventory (basename): response.txt.

Notation and limitations
This is a very tentative visual reading. The image contains a narrow surviving portion of a column at left and a wider column at right. The left column is cut off on its left; the right column is cut off on its right. The upper writing is severely faded or abraded. The bottom physical line is clipped by the image boundary. Stains, faint ink, and the resolution make many letter shapes inseparable. I have left those stretches unreadable rather than reconstructing wording.

I number the visible physical lines from top to bottom separately within each column. A question mark applies to the preceding letter or letter sequence. A macron or tilde records a visible apparent abbreviation stroke, without asserting an expansion. The small tentative letter sequences below should not be treated as established words. No expansions are sufficiently secure to supply. There is only one image, so no overlapping crops to reconcile.

INITIALS, MARGINS, AND POSSIBLE CORRECTIONS
At R02 there is a large blue rounded initial, provisionally Q, with a descending right-hand stroke. Thin red penwork appears beside and within it. I cannot read that penwork as an independent marginal addition.
At R17 there is another large blue rounded initial, also provisionally Q. It has thin red penwork, including upright/crossing strokes within its bowl and a narrow flourish to its left. I cannot securely distinguish guide lettering from ornament there.
At L14 the left edge cuts through part of a red rounded initial or ornament. Its complete shape and letter value are unavailable.
There are apparent horizontal abbreviation strokes above several words, especially in the darker lower writing. The transcription records only a few that I can place tentatively; it is not an exhaustive inventory of abbreviation marks.
Some upper lines have dark ink over very faint or broken strokes. I cannot establish that these represent cancellations or overwriting rather than surviving parts of the original letters.
